learning: Iteration 0 gave aggregates only. Off-track limit is effectively 0.06 m for body_width below about 0.19 m, so body_width gives no leverage. Next, check whether line-loss reduction holds across s-bend and slalom seeds before changing lookahead or sensor span.
notes: Single-variable test: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, controller unchanged from iteration 0. Chosen because s-bend and slalom show high line_loss_events (1.2, 1.9) with low rms_error, which points to sensor coverage rather than steering error.
rationale: Iteration 0 produced only aggregates, no per-step telemetry. The clearest signal is on the s-bend and slalom: line_loss_events average 1.2 and 1.9 while rms_error stays low (0.017 and 0.027), and runs end off track. On the oval, rms_error is 0.0105 with 16 of 20 finishes, so the controller is tracking adequately where the line stays visible. Per the Builder's intent, I am changing one variable only: sensor_size goes from 0.012 to 0.016 with x positions, y lookahead, track, wheels, body and mass unchanged. Each footprint then overlaps its neighbours more, so at least one sensor should keep reading tape through tight bends. I am also keeping the controller identical to iteration 0 (weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], kp 4, ki 0.1, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, last_direction). This keeps the race a clean test of the footprint change, and the baseline gains already gave low oscillation (0.28 to 0.35) and no controller errors. The expected result is line_loss_events below about 0.5 on the s-bend and slalom, a higher s-bend finish rate, and no worse oscillation on the oval. Body_width is not changed because the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m for any body width up to about 0.19 m. The 16 mm footprint is inside the allowed sensor_size set, and the sensor positions are inside their limits.
